finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF. The server fetches a user-supplied URL with file_get_contents. The response is not returned, but its byte length is echoed, so this is a semi-blind SSRF. It can be used to probe internal hosts and ports, reach cloud metadata endpoints, and time or size-fingerprint responses. Other PHP stream wrappers (file://, php://, ftp://, and gopher-like http requests) are also accepted.

trace.note: Reached on any POST request that has a 'feed' parameter. No authentication check.
$_POST['feed'] is passed unchanged to file_get_contents(), which performs the outbound request.
strlen($xml) is echoed to the attacker, giving an oracle for response size and for whether the fetch succeeded.

finding.guards_checked: There is no scheme or host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, and no DNS-resolution pinning. require_admin() is defined at line 4 but is not called on this path. The session is started but not checked. allow_url_fopen is assumed to be at its default of on.

verdict.reason: import.php:12 passes $_POST['feed'] unchanged to file_get_contents() and import.php:13 echoes strlen($xml), with no auth check (require_admin() at line 4 is only called at line 18) and no scheme or host validation anywhere on the path.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF. A user-supplied webhook URL is passed to curl_init and executed with curl_exec. No scheme or destination validation is applied, so an admin (or an attacker with an admin session, such as through CSRF or a hijacked session) can make the server request internal services or metadata endpoints. curl also accepts schemes such as gopher://, file://, dict:// and ftp:// by default. The response body is not returned, so this is blind SSRF.
finding.source: $_POST['set_webhook'] (HTTP POST parameter, requires an admin session)

trace.note: Branch is taken when 'set_webhook' is present in the POST data.
require_admin() is called. It only checks $_SESSION['is_admin'].

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check at lines 4-9 and 18. It limits who can reach the sink, but it does not validate the destination. There is no CSRF token, no scheme restriction (CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS is not set), no host or IP allowlist, and no CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION restriction. Redirects are not followed by default, which is a minor mitigation. Severity is lower than SSRF-1 because of the admin gate.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 and :18 (session is_admin check). It gates access but does not validate the URL, so there is no destination guard.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (import.php:17-22), but the sink at import.php:20-22 is reachable only after require_admin() at import.php:18, so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot supply the value. By the source-check rule, an admin-only input does not count as attacker-controlled.
